races.name: Reichhartinger Rush Handicap

runners_data.name: Spit Spot
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning to flat after wind operation, 15 days since disappointing here over shorter
runners_data.comment: Lost her way over hurdles this year and struggled on recent Flat return
runners_data.spotlight: Won two 3m hurdles last autumn but has lost her way over jumps this year and was well beaten here (1m4f) when back on the Flat a fortnight ago, after a wind op; this longer trip ought to suit better but it still takes a leap of faith to support her.

runners_data.name: Simple Star
runners_data.note: Proven hold-up horse, 40 days off but trainer in good form and 2lb lower than when second here
runners_data.spotlight: Soundly beaten on both Flat starts this year (1m4f/2m), and just a respectable fifth over hurdles 12 days ago; now 2lb lower than when second here (2m2f, good) last summer but needs to up his game.

runners_data.name: Elemental Eye
runners_data.note: Strong closer who won emphatically here in October, but hasn't recaptured that form in two starts since
runners_data.spotlight: Two wins last season, the latter gained by 10l here (1m6f, soft; also suited by much quicker ground) in October; not in same form on either outing since returned to the Flat in March (1m4f/2m; cheekpieces refitted last time) but still considered.

runners_data.name: Cascade Hall
runners_data.note: Front-runner coming off breakthrough win at Ayr, likely to track or challenge Velvet Whisper early
runners_data.comment: Nicked Ayr race from the front last month but backed up that run with a creditable second
runners_data.spotlight: Soon in a clear lead and perhaps stole a four-runner race at Ayr (1m7f, good to firm) on seasonal debut, belatedly opening his account; however, he backed up that performance with a clear second at Carlisle (1m6f, soft) a fortnight later and remains well handicapped on some of last year's form.

runners_data.name: Velvet Whisper
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with two wins from the lead last season, struggles more on good ground this year
runners_data.spotlight: Ended last season with two slow-ground wins from the front (1m2f/1m4f); not yet fully exposed but has been safely held twice on good ground this year (1m4f/1m2f) and is not bred for this new trip.

runners_data.name: Kisiyra
runners_data.note: Prominent racer back quickly after poor effort, claimer takes valuable weight off but form questionable
runners_data.comment: Ran pretty well on sole outing of last season but returns from another absence today
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Irish maiden; seen only once in 2025, when fourth of six at Thirsk (1m4f, good) on stable debut a year ago; back from another layoff when weakening badly with a first-time tongue-tie at Hamilton (1m5f) on Thursday.

runners_data.name: Star Of Markinch
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse winless in 44 attempts, best recent effort was fourth here two starts back
runners_data.comment: 0-44 under all codes (including three points); 10lb wrong; can't be recommended
runners_data.spotlight: 0-44 under all codes (including three points); gave pretty good account when fourth of nine here (1m4f, good) two starts ago and will be fine over today's trip but can't be recommended from 10lb out of the weights.

races.paceDynamic: Velvet Whisper will take this small field along from the front with minimal early pressure, as most rivals prefer to settle behind. Cascade Hall showed front-running tactics when winning at Ayr and may track or challenge early, but the overall tempo should be manageable through the first mile. With five of seven runners carrying hold-up styles, the pace will likely be steady rather than searching, allowing the leaders to dictate terms. This setup strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can avoid the scramble behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If Velvet Whisper gets an uncontested lead with Cascade Hall settling behind.
scenarios.body: The pace becomes too comfortable for the hold-up brigade to reel in, and the leaders kick clear turning for home. Front-runners exploit the tactical advantage over a field full of closers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closer Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely slow and the field bunches entering the straight.
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get the perfect setup to unleash finishing kicks over the final three furlongs. Simple Star and Elemental Eye benefit most from a tactical race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Backfire
scenarios.trigger: If Cascade Hall and Velvet Whisper engage in early battle for the lead.
scenarios.body: Both front-runners compromise each other's chances through the opening mile, setting up the race for closers. The tactical advantage swings completely to those held up behind.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the market leaders fail to handle the 2m trip or going conditions.
scenarios.body: Form horses disappoint and a bigger price benefits from the race shape. Star Of Markinch or Spit Spot capitalizes on the others' shortcomings.

watchPoints.text: Velvet Whisper could get too easy a lead if Cascade Hall settles behind rather than challenging
Simple Star returning from 40-day break with claimer aboard after mixed flat form this season
Elemental Eye won by 10 lengths here in October but form has tailed off since returning
Cascade Hall may not handle step up from winning over 1m7f to today's 2m trip
Three apprentice/conditional jockeys aboard in small field could create tactical confusion

races.name: Menzies Meander EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B-D) (EBF Restricted Qual') (GBB/IRE Incentive)

runners_data.name: Mr Minz
runners_data.note: Unknown running style but lightly raced status makes him a wildcard for Charlie Johnston's stable despite modest recent strike-rate
runners_data.comment: Closely related to a 6f 2yo winner; would be rare first-time-out 2yo winner for stable
runners_data.spotlight: 70,000euros yearling; second foal; closely related to 6f 2yo winner French Affair (RPR 78); dam a modest four-race maiden (64); stable has very modest strike-rate with first-time-out 2yos.

runners_data.name: Odegaard
runners_data.note: Unproven style and another lightly raced type who could benefit from the expected honest gallop if he has any ability
runners_data.comment: Half-brother to fair 1m2f handicapper and dual 1m winner; yard not known for 2yo winners
runners_data.spotlight: Half-brother to fair middle-distance handicapper Lethal Touch and dual 1m winner Vondelpark; dam unraced half-sister to three useful winners; already gelded; stable not known for 2yo winners.

runners_data.name: Time For The Moon
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader whose recent Haydock third came in a slowly run race, so this stronger pace should suit better
runners_data.comment: Well-bred colt; close third of four in slowly run race on debut at Haydock
runners_data.spotlight: Well-bred colt who was close third of four in slowly run contest at Haydock (7f, good to soft; 11-10f) a fortnight ago; that form is tricky to evaluate but, if his pedigree is a guide, a stronger pace over this trip ought to show him in a better light.

runners_data.name: Heldobeldo
runners_data.note: Front runner who impressed on AW debut and the step up to 7f on turf should enhance his stamina strengths
runners_data.comment: Made promising debut when close second of ten at Kempton (6f, AW) last month; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Out of a half-sister to an Italian Listed 2yo winner; made promising debut when close second of ten at Kempton (6f, AW) last month and has big role to play if suited by this different trip-and-ground combination.

runners_data.name: Tribal Appearance
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has faced Time For The Moon before and can use that experience to sit closer to the pace
runners_data.comment: Not beaten far on either outing (5.7f/7f), albeit both those races were slowly run
runners_data.spotlight: Second of five on last month's debut at Bath (5.7f, firm) and not beaten far when last of four (just behind Time For The Moon) in another slowly run contest at Haydock (7f, good to soft) a fortnight ago; no surprise if he's on the premises again here.

runners_data.name: Amantha
runners_data.note: Prominent type whose Beverley sixth showed improved form, but her tendency to fade in the finish remains a concern
runners_data.comment: Soundly beaten over 5f on first two starts but recent 7.4f run was much more encouraging
runners_data.spotlight: Soundly beaten over 5f on first two starts but her recent sixth at Beverley (7.4f, good to firm) was much more encouraging; further progress will almost certainly be required here, though.

races.paceDynamic: Time For The Moon and Heldobeldo are confirmed front runners who will engage from the start, creating an honest gallop over this 7f trip. With only six runners, the early pace battle between these two leaders should create a genuine test rather than a crawl. This sustained gallop will set up the race for horses that can sit prominently and finish, as the two leaders may compromise each other. The race shape strongly favors prominent racers who can track the pace and late runners who can capitalize on any early speed duel.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leaders Compromise Each Other
scenarios.trigger: If Time For The Moon and Heldobeldo engage in a sustained speed duel from flag-fall
scenarios.body: The two front runners will burn each other out over the 7f trip, creating the perfect setup for closers to pick up the pieces. This tactical scenario heavily favors hold-up horses and those that can sit off the pace and time their runs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If either Time For The Moon or Heldobeldo gets an uncontested lead while the other settles
scenarios.body: The lone leader will dictate terms and prove hard to peg back in this small field, especially with the good going providing ideal conditions for front runners. Prominent racers tracking the leader will be best placed to challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Modest Early Pace
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders are more restrained early and the pace becomes pedestrian
scenarios.body: A slowly run race will become a sprint finish where the best turn of foot wins, negating any tactical advantages. This compressed finish will suit horses with natural speed regardless of running style.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Tribal Appearance can secure the perfect tracking position behind the leaders
scenarios.body: The Bath runner-up can use his proven tactical speed to sit in the ideal spot and outkick the front runners when it matters. His prominent style perfectly suits tracking two confirmed pace-setters.

watchPoints.text: Time For The Moon and Heldobeldo must be watched for how aggressively they go forward as their early battle will dictate the entire race shape
Mr Minz and Odegaard are both lightly raced unknowns who could surprise if they have any latent ability for their experienced handlers
Tribal Appearance's positioning behind the leaders will be crucial as he needs to avoid getting trapped if the pace becomes too strong
The early fractions will reveal whether this becomes a true test or develops into a sprint finish that changes all calculations

races.name: Construction & Property Recruitment Handicap

runners_data.name: Stoic Poet
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suited to expected pace scenario, proven at this distance and recent good form suggests he's ready to strike
runners_data.comment: Good second on soft ground last month; significant rain will make him of interest
runners_data.spotlight: Two good runs this season, latterly when keeping-on second in Haydock handicap (7f, soft) a fortnight ago; ought to make his presence felt again here, and significant rain will increase his appeal.

runners_data.name: Highland Shah
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who faces traffic dangers with multiple others wanting same position, first-time hood adds unknown element
runners_data.comment: Encouraging fourth in Catterick novice on seasonal debut; open to improvement in handicaps
runners_data.spotlight: In the frame all three starts, most recently when fourth of 11 (behind Sandy Craic) on last month's seasonal debut at Catterick (7f, good; first-time hood); should have some improvement to come in handicaps; no surprise if he features.

runners_data.name: Sandy Craic
runners_data.note: Still maiden despite multiple placings, prominent style puts her in the danger zone but solid York fifth shows ability
runners_data.spotlight: Still a maiden after seven starts but was placed twice (6f/7f) before her very respectable fifth of 20 at York (7f, good) a fortnight ago; big player in this easier race if first-time cheekpieces have any positive effect.

runners_data.name: Yorkshire Queen
runners_data.note: Prominent style clashes with others, disappointing when upped in trip suggests 7f is her limit
runners_data.comment: Raced too freely and disappointed when upped to 1m; quickly drops back to 7f
runners_data.spotlight: Seven-race maiden; made quite promising seasonal debut when fourth at Southwell (7f, AW) last month but raced too freely and was disappointing when upped to 1m at Haydock (good to soft) a fortnight ago; drops back to 7f with a point to prove.

runners_data.name: Wise Crack
runners_data.note: Hold-up style gives tactical advantage, 5lb claimer reduces weight burden, return to 7f should suit better than recent 6f efforts
runners_data.comment: 0-6 but latest run was much better than stable debut, and this return to 7f will suit
runners_data.spotlight: Six-race maiden; bettered inauspicious seasonal/stable debut when fifth of eight at Doncaster (6f, good to soft) last month and, with this return to 7f likely to suit, could plausibly take another step forward here.

runners_data.name: Homestrait
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with course and distance win, cheekpieces help but trainer's poor recent form is concerning
runners_data.comment: More exposed than some of these but ran well in defeat in new cheekpieces last month
runners_data.spotlight: Dual 2yo winner (once over C&D); more exposed than some of these but ran game race from the front when close second in first-time cheekpieces at Catterick (7f, good) a fortnight ago; contender if headgear continues to aid.

runners_data.name: The Anthony Gover
runners_data.note: Fellow pace-setter means early battle likely, blinkers retained after handicap debut, remains relatively unexposed
runners_data.comment: Just a respectable sixth when dropped to 7f for handicap debut but remains unexposed
runners_data.spotlight: Just a respectable sixth when dropped to 7f and fitted with blinkers (retained) for recent handicap debut at Wolverhampton (AW) but remains unexposed and a recent 2lb drop helps.

runners_data.name: Born A Star
runners_data.note: Course and distance winner but tendency to race too freely could be fatal in this pace setup
runners_data.comment: C&D maiden winner last summer but disappointing in all three handicaps this year
runners_data.spotlight: Won C&D (good) maiden last summer but has disappointed in all three handicaps this season (7f-8.6f) and his tendency to race too freely remains a worry; needs to get career back on track.

runners_data.name: Maximum Velocity
runners_data.note: Recent winner who races from rear, 5lb rise makes task harder but style suits the likely scenario
runners_data.comment: Made all at Redcar recently but his tendency to race too freely remains a nagging concern
runners_data.spotlight: Made all to open account at Redcar (7f, good) last month, his eighth start, but recent 5lb rise demands a bit more from him here and his tendency to race too freely remains a nagging concern.

runners_data.name: Walk On Walk On
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with big weight advantage, blinkers fitted and 7f return positive but remains a maiden after nine attempts
runners_data.comment: Ran quite well in new blinkers last month; needs to build on that effort here
runners_data.spotlight: Nine-race maiden; posted by far his best of three runs for new stable this season when dropped back to 7f and tried in blinkers (retained) at Redcar (good) last month, finishing fourth; up in grade here and needs to build on that effort.

races.paceDynamic: Homestrait and The Anthony Gover will contest the early lead, with both front-runners likely to set an honest gallop over this 7f trip. Sandy Craic, Highland Shah, Yorkshire Queen and Born A Star all want prominent positions, creating significant congestion and potential traffic problems turning for home. The dual pace angle should create a searching test, but the presence of multiple prominent racers suggests those able to get a clear run from off the pace will have the tactical edge. This race shape favours hold-up horses who can avoid the early scrimmaging and finish strongly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent brigade gets bunched up turning for home
scenarios.body: The early pace battle between Homestrait and The Anthony Gover sets up a strong gallop, allowing closers to pick off the pace-pressured leaders. Traffic problems in the prominent pack play into the hands of those with cleaner runs from the rear.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Homestrait and The Anthony Gover get loose on the lead without pressure
scenarios.body: The two front-runners steal a march on the field and kick clear of the struggling prominent pack before the closers can get into gear. Their tactical advantage proves decisive in a race where positioning beats raw ability.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses avoid traffic and get first run
scenarios.body: Sandy Craic, Highland Shah or Born A Star manage to secure ideal positions just behind the leaders and pounce when the pace-setters weaken. Their superior tactical position allows them to hold off the late challengers despite the honest gallop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too fast and burn out completely
scenarios.body: Homestrait and The Anthony Gover set unsustainable fractions and come back dramatically, turning this into a sprint finish. The race becomes a lottery where any horse getting a trouble-free run can capitalize on the early pace sacrifice.

watchPoints.text: Watch for traffic problems at the 2f pole where Sandy Craic, Highland Shah, Yorkshire Queen and Born A Star could all converge seeking racing room
Monitor how aggressively Homestrait and The Anthony Gover battle for the early lead as excessive pace could set up a dramatic finish
Check if Born A Star settles better than usual in the early stages as his tendency to pull hard has cost him in recent handicaps
Observe whether Stoic Poet gets the clear run his hold-up style demands as traffic could nullify his tactical advantage
Watch Maximum Velocity's positioning early as his recent front-running win suggests he might adopt different tactics here

races.name: Keith Mitchell Law Accountants Handicap

runners_data.name: Poet's Dawn
runners_data.note: Veteran prominent runner who won from the front at Ripon last month but carries a 4lb penalty after failing under similar conditions
runners_data.comment: Veteran; won off reduced mark last month but held since; younger rivals preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran who exploited a reduced mark when winning from the front at Ripon (1m2f, good) last month; held under 4lb penalty soon afterwards, though, and effectively another 1lb higher here; younger rivals appeal more.

runners_data.name: Starliner
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who was unlucky when denied a clear run at Hamilton nine days ago and remains well handicapped
runners_data.comment: Looked unlucky at Hamilton recently and is still only 2lb higher than for win in early May
runners_data.spotlight: Looked unlucky when third at Hamilton (8.3f, good to firm) nine days ago, where he was persistently denied a clear run, and remains just 2lb higher than when scoring at Ayr (1m, good to firm) in early May; high on the list.

runners_data.name: Amidst The Chaos
runners_data.note: Strong closer who won twice last August including over course and distance, returning from a 24-day break
runners_data.spotlight: Gained both wins last August, the latter over C&D (good); denied clear run before making the frame at Ripon (1m, good) and Beverley (8.4f, good to firm) on last two appearances; can be dangerous if his luck changes.

runners_data.name: Union Island
runners_data.note: Front runner with two wins this year including a nose victory at Leicester, likely to face no early pace pressure
runners_data.spotlight: Two wins this year, the latter when coming from off the pace to prevail by a nose at Leicester (1m, good to firm) last month; still on a workable mark but his record is very mixed, and he didn't fire on latest outing.

runners_data.name: Mayor Of Maghera
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 442 days off after disappointing hurdles campaign, questionable fitness
runners_data.comment: Disappointing over hurdles this year and has quite a bit to prove on stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Well handicapped on some of his old Flat form for Phillip Makin but was disappointing during four-race spell over hurdles for an Irish stable this year and has quite a bit to prove on debut for Mike Smith.

runners_data.name: Dingwall
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up horse placed several times recently including close second at Ayr off today's mark
runners_data.comment: Placed several times since his two AW wins in November; below form lately, though
runners_data.spotlight: Won consecutive AW races in November (9.4f/8.6f) and has been placed several times since, including a close second off today's mark at Ayr (1m1f, good to firm) in early May; needs to get back on track after two below-par runs, though.

runners_data.name: Motawaared
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who has been uncompetitive in two starts this season and remains winless after eight attempts
runners_data.comment: Did not get seriously competitive when seventh on first two starts this season (1m4f/1m1f)
runners_data.spotlight: Did not get seriously competitive when seventh on first two starts this season (1m4f/1m1f) and is now 0-8 overall; worth a glance in the betting but others have much more obvious claims.

runners_data.name: Detective
runners_data.note: Veteran 10-year-old hold-up type with blinkers back on after being soundly beaten in both starts this year
runners_data.spotlight: 10yo who gained the latest of his eight career wins over this C&D (good; wore blinkers) last summer; soundly beaten on both outings this year but has blinkers refitted today and it won't be a shock if he stages a revival.

races.paceDynamic: Union Island and Poet's Dawn are the only horses with prominent/leading tendencies in this small field, with Union Island likely to dictate from the front given his recent front-running success. With six hold-up horses (Starliner, Amidst The Chaos, Dingwall, Motawaared, Detective, Mayor Of Maghera) sitting behind, the pace will be sustainable and tactical. Union Island faces minimal early pressure, allowing him to control fractions and kick clear when ready. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those who can sit close to the pace, as the hold-up horses will struggle to make up ground against a controlled tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Union Island gets an uncontested lead and dictates fractions
scenarios.body: Union Island faces no pace pressure early and can time his effort perfectly, while the large pack of hold-up horses gets strung out behind. The tactical advantage goes to those positioned closest to the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely slow and kick is delayed
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get the perfect setup to unleash their finishing speed in the final two furlongs. Starliner and Amidst The Chaos benefit most from their proven closing ability.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Poet's Dawn Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Poet's Dawn travels better than Union Island mid-race
scenarios.body: The veteran exploits his prominent position to strike when Union Island weakens, using his experience at this level. His recent Ripon win showed he retains ability when positioned handily.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If both prominent runners fail to sustain their effort
scenarios.body: Union Island and Poet's Dawn both weaken in the straight, creating a scrambled finish among the closers. The most progressive hold-up horse benefits from the tactical meltdown.

watchPoints.text: Union Island getting a soft lead early - if he faces no pressure through the first half-mile, he becomes very dangerous
Starliner's position turning for home - needs a clear run after being repeatedly denied at Hamilton last time
Poet's Dawn's early positioning - whether he challenges Union Island for the lead or settles behind
The gap between the front pair and the hold-up brigade at halfway - a large gap makes it harder for closers
Mayor Of Maghera's fitness after 442 days off - any market support would be significant given his long absence

races.name: Travis Perkins Edinburgh Handicap

runners_data.name: Right And Exact
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner coming off career-best form at Thirsk three weeks ago, likely to set a strong pace but may be vulnerable to multiple challengers
runners_data.comment: Led close home to take 17-runner Thirsk handicap last month and is now 2-5
runners_data.spotlight: Low-mileage 4yo who led close home to take 17-runner Thirsk handicap (5f, good) three weeks ago and is now 2-5; probably still has more to offer and commands respect.

runners_data.name: Curious Rover
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with course and distance win on good ground, blinkers retained after disappointing AW run but drops 2lbs in weight
runners_data.comment: Slightly disappointing on AW last week but previous turf run gives him each-way claims
runners_data.spotlight: Gained last season's win over C&D (good); slightly disappointing in first-time blinkers (retained) on AW a week ago but now 2lb lower than when fourth of 17 behind Right And Exact at Thirsk (5f, good) two starts ago.

runners_data.name: Tiva
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer needing pace collapse, fitted with tongue-tie and visor after solid Hamilton second nine days ago
runners_data.comment: Remains on a fairly tough mark but posted sound effort when second at Hamilton recently
runners_data.spotlight: Built upon satisfactory seasonal debut when second of six in refitted tongue-tie/visor at Hamilton (5f, good to firm) nine days ago; still on a fairly tough mark but can make her presence felt again.

runners_data.name: Miss Brazen
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits this track perfectly, 7lb claimer takes off valuable weight after excellent Beverley third 24 days back
runners_data.comment: Scored on seasonal debut and ran at least as well when close third next time; up in grade
runners_data.spotlight: Made winning seasonal debut under Lewis Chalkley at Nottingham (5f, good) in April and ran at least as well when close third at Beverley (5f, good to firm) last month; up in grade today but evidently in good nick.

runners_data.name: I'm Next
runners_data.note: Tactical prominent racer with excellent Beverley form in April, proven course winner who can adapt to pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Good winner at Beverley in April and ran well in quite valuable C&D contest next time
runners_data.spotlight: Showed career-best form when winning comfortably at Beverley (5f, good) in April and again ran well when fourth of 12 in quite valuable C&D (good) contest three days later; will beaten in good-quality York handicap since but back in calmer waters here and goes on the shortlist.

runners_data.name: Woohoo
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with two course wins including one on good ground, needs strong pace but ran well at Thirsk just five days ago
runners_data.comment: Dual C&D winner; in good form but current mark demands a career-best effort
runners_data.spotlight: Gained two of his five wins over C&D, the latter on good ground in April; didn't run badly in a big field at Thirsk (5f, good) on Sunday but current mark demands a career-best performance.

runners_data.name: Lion's House
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner better on artificial surfaces, struggles on turf with poor course record over this distance
runners_data.comment: Tapeta is his surface and finished well behind in his last two races on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time AW winner; went close on Tapeta at Newcastle (5f) last month but finished well down the field either side on turf and only fourth of six at Hamilton on Thursday; not the percentage call.

runners_data.name: Little Mi Mi
runners_data.note: Confirmed hold-up horse moving up significantly in class after three lower-grade wins, needs everything to fall right
runners_data.spotlight: Resurgent mare who has collected three wins this year, two on Newcastle AW and the latest at Ayr (5f, good to firm) last month; they were Class 6 races, though, and she was soundly beaten when recently upped to Class 3.

races.paceDynamic: Right And Exact will set the pace from the start with several prominent racers including Curious Rover, Miss Brazen, and I'm Next tracking close behind, creating a competitive but not unsustainable gallop over this straight 5f course. The substantial group of hold-up horses (Tiva, Woohoo, Lion's House, Little Mi Mi) will need to rely on the pace collapsing or finding racing room in the final furlong. With multiple front-runners likely to press Right And Exact and several proven over course and distance, this pace setup strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the pace and strike in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong but sustainable with Right And Exact pressed by multiple rivals
scenarios.body: The pace-setters will weaken slightly in the final 100 yards, allowing those tracking in second and third positions to strike. Horses like Miss Brazen and I'm Next, both proven at this trip with tactical speed, can time their runs perfectly from these positions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Right And Exact goes too fast early under pressure from multiple prominent racers
scenarios.body: The early leaders will tie up dramatically in the final furlong, creating opportunities for the hold-up horses to sweep past. Tiva's class and Woohoo's course form become decisive factors when the pace falls apart.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Right And Exact Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Right And Exact gets an uncontested lead with rivals reluctant to press early
scenarios.body: The favourite will be allowed to dictate terms and kick clear when asked, using superior class to hold off late challenges. His recent Thirsk win suggests he has more improvement in him at this mark.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Speed Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely run throughout with no collapse and sustained pressure
scenarios.body: Horses with both early speed and finishing kick will prove superior to pure pace-setters and pure closers. The race becomes a test of tactical versatility rather than pure running style.

races.paceDynamic: Lope Y Linda will set the pace from the front with minimal pressure, as all other runners have hold-up or midfield styles. The front runner can dictate a comfortable gallop through the early stages before quickening in the final three furlongs. With five hold-up horses (Mereside Princess, Bobbys Pride, Longevity, Saxon Gem, Royal Baroness) all needing to come from behind, Lope Y Linda faces no early pressure and can control the tempo completely. This race shape strongly favours the front runner and any horse that can track close early, as the lack of pace pressure creates a tactical advantage for forward positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Lope Y Linda gets an easy lead and dictates fractions
scenarios.body: The pace-setter controls the race from flag to finish, kicking clear when the hold-up horses are still organizing their challenges. Forward runners benefit from the soft fractions and positional advantage over the congested pack behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Charge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too slow and bunches the field
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get their preferred scenario with a sprint finish from the back, overwhelming a front runner who went too slow early. Mereside Princess and Royal Baroness benefit from their proven stamina at this trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Lope Y Linda stops quickly after controlling early
scenarios.body: The lone pace-setter hits the wall in the final furlong after dictating throughout, allowing the strongest finisher from the pack to sweep past. The winner emerges from the trailing group who conserved energy behind the soft pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Bunching
scenarios.trigger: If jockeys hold up too much and create traffic problems
scenarios.body: Multiple hold-up horses find trouble in running as they all come with late runs simultaneously, benefiting those who avoided the scrimmaging. Clear passage becomes crucial when six runners converge in the final two furlongs.

watchPoints.text: Lope Y Linda could steal this if she gets uncontested fractions and the hold-up brigade leave their runs too late
Traffic problems likely in straight as five hold-up horses converge simultaneously from similar positions
Bobbys Pride returning after 264 days with concerning finishing tendencies could struggle if pace quickens
Saxon Gem stepping up in trip after 6f debut may need this longer distance to show her true ability
Apprentice claim on Longevity provides weight advantage but inexperience could cost in tactical battle
